name: Three-Act Structure
summary: Setup, confrontation and resolution: establish the world, escalate the conflict, then resolve it and land the message.

sequence.purpose: Act one: the setup and the world.
Act one ends: the inciting incident.
Mark the move into act two.
Act two: rising conflict and attempts.

pitfalls: A long setup that delays the conflict.
A second act that repeats instead of escalating.
A resolution with no message attached.

example.topic: A fictional town library winning back its readers
outline: How a small library found its readers again
The library had shelves full and halls empty
The council threatened to cut its budget
Late opening hours drew in night-shift workers
Visits doubled in the month of the budget vote
Meet people where their day already is
